My first use making a pork roast tasted like I cooked in indoors in an oven. I was initially going to return it to Home Depot where I bought it but decided because of ease of use to continue using my new Spirit gas grill.  I am tired of the mess of using charcoal and having to wait for my fire to be ready to cook on.  I plan on experimenting with trying to get a better smoke taste.  If I have to use a smoke box, I might as well have bought a charcoal grill.  Home Depot was kind enough to let me try it for three months with the option of returning it if I am not satisfied so I am glad I bought it from them.  Putting butter or oil on meats seems to help with the smoke taste as it causes a flare of flames to help with achieving the smoke taste.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
It’s been about two months and I have grilled this summer between 2-3 times a week. I got it from Amazon who offered me to pay in 5 installments and had free delivery + free assembly. Great deal.

The grill fit perfectly in my balcony, which is about 5ft wide with both side trays. Assemble this grill took an experienced guy around 4hrs. 

Pros: 
- Good fit for most balconies if you live in an apartment 
- Quickly start grilling 15 min
- Disposable dripping pan allows to collect fat, grease and dirt
- Two trays keep sufficient space for your tools and those ready to grill meats. Trays also have three tools hangers each side for a total of six
- Ability to connect Weber Bluetooth thermometer. Not sure I need this but it is available
- Three burners allow to control temp and grill with direct or indirect heat 
- I grilled a NY Steak. 1 ¼” thick. It was awesome (see picture)
- It greatly reduces smoke, which may be an issue if you live in an apartment, however, it depends on how much fat your meats can have
- The fire starter is really convenient and I haven’t had any issues 

Cons:
- Definitely cleaning the grill is not one of my favorite. I think I should clean it after 5-6. If you have a patio, cleaning shouldn’t be that difficult 
- The gas regulator that connects to the tank had a leak out if the box, hopefully the Weber support replaced it quickly at no cost and now it working like charm
Results.Title: First Gas Grill (Spirit II - E-310)

Grilling great steaks, burgers and chicken and more!

Results.ReviewText: I bought this grill to replace my Weber grill that I've  had for 20 yrs. The old one still works good but it was time for a change. This new one heats up in a flash. Gets hotter than the old one ever did. In some ways its better. But in some ways its not. Its not as heavy duty as they used to be. Even the cast iron grills are much lighter duty than the older ones. I swapped out the grills from the old to the new grill. They fit perfectly  and they're  3 years old, so theyre in great shape. The one thing I don't  like about this new grill is the noise it makes from the burners. It makes a fluttering noise similar  to the noise when you're  running out of gas. You can hear it the whole time its running. Its a little annoying. Customer service  said its normal  they all make that noise. Overall Im happy with the grill. I dont know if it will last 20 yrs. like my old one did. But I think  Webers are still the best buy for the money.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I did a TON of research online before buying this and am extremely happy with it! My last 3 grills had all suffered from intense rusting of some major part and I was sick of dealing with it and spending $300 every 5 years on new grills and parts for those grills to keep them going. This thing is made of cast aluminum and/or other powder-coated metals so the only uncoated metal is in the burners. The open shelves eliminate a hiding place for wasps & spiders and make it easy to grab things there or place things there. The integrated fuel gauge eliminates guesswork on "how much propane do I have". It is very sturdy in case you need to move it (I elected to assemble it myself to ensure it's sturdy). There is minimal venting so heat stays inside to cook your food thoroughly. You can add the i3 temperature sensor system if you like. Cleanup is easy: scrub the grate with a steel brush right after you finish cooking, use a stainless steel wipe on the sides and control panel, then use a wipe to clean off the top and shelves. Cover it when it’s cool and it will probably last decades! We use this at least once a week and the whole family looks forward to grilling meals! Pro-tip: keep Weber’s grilling guide open in a browser tab on your phone for quick reference so you cook everything properly – this grill uses page 3. (weber.com/US/ne/help/assets/pdf/GrillingGuide.pdf)

Photos.Caption: Epic move and I still haven’t found the missing knob.

Results.ReviewText:
I needed to completely furnish a fairly remote summer home I purchased in the mountains. Furnishings were purchased and loaded on a fully packed Uhaul truck and that included a new Weber grill. Somewhere in the 800 mile move I lost one of the burner knobs. Looking on the Weber website for the part, I came up empty so I called to order one. Explaining my situation to the patient customer service rep she offered to mail me one free of charge even though it was clearly not a warranty issue. That’s truly taking care of your customers! Most buyers will never need any service for their grill, but it’s great to know it’s there if you need it. 

Weber rocks! Thank you.
Results.Title: Service after the sale.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: Weber grills are amazing.  This grill has ample grilling space and gets very warm because of the three gas runs.  I firmly believe there is a small design flaw that affects us because we move the grill in and out of the garage to use.  The drop down shelf on the left side is the side that you use to move the grill.  The shelf doesn't stay in place when pressure (from moving the grill) is applied.  Either the screw is too short and needs to be longer, or the metal shelf needs reinforced so it stays square.  That being said, I called and the Weber representative was amazing to work with, and she was able to send replacement parts right away.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
After 13 or so years of solid useI had to lay my previous Spirit E-310 to rest. It was a sad moment for us. It was truly a member of our family. So I decided to purchase another based on how WELL our previous was built and how LONG it lasted. I again, like I did previous, purchased the newer Spirit II form a "big Box" store because I wanted one that I could put together myself right out of the box. I personally feel like that is part of the overall experience and there is no better way to really get to know your grill than when you have a hand in giving it life. Or, I just have a ton of time on my hands. Here are a few observations that may or may not help you in deciding if this is the right grill for you. Outside of the basics, here are a few Pros & Cons from my camera angle...

Pros: 
1) Easy to assemble - took about an hour. 
2) Low Profile Lid - I dig it.
3) 2 Stainless Steel Shelves -munch better than the older plastic ones
4) Large Control Knobs
5) Electronic Ignition - although it doesn't ignite right away from some reason.
6) Flame Bar & Flavorizer Design & Layout.
7) 10 Year Warranty
8) We are big fans of Weber in General

Cons (with some explanations for clarity):
1) Warming Rack Does Not Fit - one out of the box and the replacement rack are too wide to "easily" slide into place as the manual noted. 
2) Not Easy to Move Grill - shelve used to move grill is foldable. when you lift to move the shovel comes unhinged which is utterly annoying. 
3) Lower Box of Grill was Warped on Left Side Out of the Box - left side of lower heat box was warped and as result, grates do not sit flat and lid does not sit flush. Which in turn allows heat to escape would assume. Also could be a factor in why the warming rack doesn't fit.
4) Flames Are Inconsistent - Burns orange/yellow more than blue. 

With all that said, It's an okay grill and I can see why it comes with a 10 year warranty.
Not sure it's worth what we paid but after 10+ cooks on it, it does the job in spite of some of the concerns I may have.  It may be goos to note that we also have a pellet smoker that we use on occasion but for us and our lifestyle, gas is where its at. If you are in a position to afford it, I would recommend the Genesis line. Better quality.
Results.Title: Not Quite What It Could/Should Be for the Money
